transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... I guess the main thing that pushed me to come in is, well, it's probably just a bad habit, but I've been having a little bit of trouble at work. I process insurance claims, and I just... I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Like, even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, I end up leaving my seat and walking around. 

I really want to do a good job there, and I know I should just sit and do the work, so I figured I should probably talk to someone about it. I hope I'm not wasting your time with something so small, but... does that sound like an okay reason to be here?

When you get up and walk around, do you feel like you are doing it because you have a specific, recurring thought or a sense that something isn't 'right' if you don't move, or is it more just that you feel restless and have trouble focusing on the task?

Um, that's a really good question. I don't think it's a specific thought, really. Like, I don't feel like something bad is going to happen or that things aren't 'right'... at least, I haven't noticed anything like that. I hope I'm understanding what you mean correctly. 

I guess it's more just... my mind kind of drifts off the claims I'm reading, and I just feel a little, um, antsy? Like I just need to stretch my legs for a second. It's probably just me being a little undisciplined with my focus, to be honest. I just sort of find myself up and getting water or walking to the printer before I even really realize I've stopped working. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Outside of these moments at work, would you describe yourself as someone who generally worries a lot or finds it hard to control your concerns about everyday things?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I guess I worry a normal amount, just like anybody else does about paying bills or doing a good job. But I wouldn't say I'm a super anxious person or anything like that. I don't feel like I'm constantly worried about everyday things. 

I try to keep a pretty positive attitude, mostly. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just... I don't want to make it sound like I'm overwhelmed by worry, because I'm really not. I just have that little bit of trouble staying in my seat at work. Does that sound normal to you?
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, did you experience these same kinds of struggles with staying seated or focusing on your tasks?

Um... well, I guess if I really think about it... it's not entirely a new thing. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I was a bad student or a troublemaker, because I always tried to be good! But, um, back in elementary school, my teachers used to write notes on my report cards saying that I was a bright kid—which was always really nice of them to say—but that I, well, I guess I lost my worksheets a lot. 

And they'd mention that I sometimes missed instructions or needed a few extra reminders to actually finish my classwork. I always just thought I was a little disorganized, you know, just normal kid stuff? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it was. I really did want to do well in school. Does that kind of answer your question?
In your daily life, do you often find that you make careless mistakes in your tasks because you have difficulty paying close attention to details?

Um, well... I guess maybe sometimes? I mean, I really try my best to be careful, especially with the claims, because I know it's important. I definitely wouldn't say I'm careless on purpose or anything like that. 

But, um, I suppose there are times when I might miss a small detail here or there. Like, maybe I misread a date or skip over a line if I'm trying to get through a big stack of files. I always try to catch it, though! I think everyone makes little slip-ups sometimes, right? It's just... maybe I have to double-check my work a little more often than some other people. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee. Does that seem like a normal amount of mistakes to you?
In your conversations with friends or colleagues, do you often find yourself blurting out answers before they have finished asking their questions?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really try to be polite and listen to what people have to say, especially at work. I know it's important to be respectful of everyone's time and let them finish their thoughts. 

I mean, maybe once in a great while if I'm just super excited about a topic or we're just joking around, I might jump in a little quick? But I definitely wouldn't say I make a habit of interrupting people or blurting things out. I always try to wait my turn. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was rude or anything like that. That's pretty normal, right? To just wait until someone is done talking?
In your daily life, do you find that your attention is easily diverted by things happening around you, like background noises or other people's conversations?

Um, well... I guess I can get a little sidetracked sometimes, but I really try to stay focused, especially when I'm working on claims. I know how important it is to keep my mind on what I'm doing. 

But, um, I suppose if the people near me start talking about another claim, or... or if I just suddenly remember some random errand I need to run later, my attention might kind of, well, slide off what I'm reading. And then I might have to reread the same section a few times just to make sure I got it right. I always make sure I understand it eventually, though! I just want to do a good job. I think it's pretty normal to get a little distracted when it's noisy, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm not paying attention to my work.
When you are in social or work situations, do you often find it very difficult to remain seated for long periods, such as during long meetings or at the movies?

Um, well... I guess, yeah, maybe a little bit? Actually, um... to be completely honest, that's kind of the main thing that pushed me to come in and see you. I'm a little embarrassed to admit it, because I know how it sounds, but... I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. 

Like, I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, and I really, really try to! But I just end up needing to get up to stretch my legs or grab water or just... move, I guess. I always try to make up for the time, though, I promise. I definitely don't want my supervisors to think I'm a bad worker or that I'm slacking off, because I really care about doing a good job. It's just... it's just hard to stay glued to the chair sometimes. Sitting at a desk all day is tough for a lot of people, right? Do you think that makes me sound like a terrible employee?

Aside from getting up to walk around, do you often find that you feel physically restless in other ways, such as feeling the need to constantly fidget with your hands, tap your feet, or move around even when you are sitting down?

Um, well... I guess I might do that a little bit? I mean, I really try to sit still and look professional, especially when we have trainings or those longer team meetings. I know it's important to look like you're paying attention and respecting the presenter.

But, um, I suppose if the meeting goes on for a while, I might... I don't know, maybe bounce my leg a little under the table? Or sometimes I catch myself clicking my pen, or just kind of shifting around in my chair a bit. I always try to stop as soon as I realize I'm doing it, though! I really don't want to distract anyone else or make it seem like I'm not engaged, because I really am trying to focus. It's just a way to kind of burn off a little nervous energy, I guess. That's pretty common, isn't it? To fidget just a tiny bit during a long meeting? I hope it doesn't make me look unprofessional.
Outside of the things we've already discussed, do you often find yourself losing things necessary for tasks or activities, such as your keys, glasses, phone, or important work documents?

Um, well... I guess I do misplace things every now and then, but I really try to stay organized. I know how important it is to keep track of everything, especially with all the sensitive information we handle. 

But, um... to be honest, I suppose I do find myself hunting for things I just had a little more often than I'd like to admit. Like, sometimes I'll set down a claim form, or my headset, or... or even just a sticky note with a callback number on it, and then I turn around and I just can't find it. And, um, there have been a few times where I've temporarily lost my access badge, which is super embarrassing. I always find everything eventually, though! I'm really careful to retrace my steps and make sure nothing is actually lost. I just... I think sometimes my desk gets a little cluttered when I'm working hard, you know? It's pretty normal to misplace a pen or a note when you're busy, right? I really hope it doesn't make me sound careless or irresponsible.
In your daily life, do you often find yourself feeling as though you are 'driven by a motor' or needing to be constantly on the go?

Um, no, I don't think so. Not really. I mean, I know I just said I get up from my desk and fidget a little bit, but I definitely don't feel like I have a motor inside me or anything extreme like that. 

When I'm off the clock or just at home, I can totally just relax on the couch and watch a show or whatever. I don't feel like I constantly have to be running around or going somewhere. I'm actually pretty calm most of the time! I hope that makes sense? Like, it's really just the sitting at the workstation for eight hours straight that gets to me, but I'm not, you know, bouncing off the walls or completely out of control. That's a good sign, right? That I can still just relax and be still when I'm in my own space?

Looking at your daily life overall, would you say that your struggles with staying focused and organized are more prominent and frequent than your struggles with feeling restless or needing to move around?

Um, yeah, I think that's probably fair to say. I mean, I really do try my best to keep everything together and stay on top of my work, but... yeah, the focus and the organizing things are definitely what trip me up the most. 

The moving around stuff, like the fidgeting or getting up from my desk, it's really just a minor thing, you know? It's not a big deal at all. But trying to keep track of all the claim files and remember what step I'm on when the phone rings... that's where I feel like I struggle a bit more. Even though I really put a lot of effort into it! I just... I want to do a good job, and it's frustrating when my brain kind of wanders off. But it's definitely more of an attention thing than a physical energy thing, if that makes sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
